flags.observation: "rings the bell before Freud counts" barely condenses the deck thesis (Id kicks out at two, couch as mat); the listener gets little onboarding.
Callback to bell and seat lands, but "That bell still rings beside the empty seat." gives mood, not a provocative satirical turn.
"But the crib waits" comes three beats after "But Freud wishes"; the But-family opens five lines, two within ten lines.
"So another tooth" is the third So-opener at eight-beat spacing after "So downstairs" and "So yesterday"; family spacing under ten lines.
"So hunger" claims causation from The Interpretation Detective that the sequence does not earn; the connector is formal, not a real therefore.
Opener "Lie down:" duplicates the card's own "lie down" at once; an echo, not a bridge building on The Rebus.
"Dad's law" appears as opener and again as the line's tail; same doubling with "downstairs" in beat 3 and "hunger" in beat 43.
Tail "redaction" is a bare power label; the pattern recurs ("symbolic authority", "surrender", "projection", "stuck", "control") and reads as length padding.
Opener "Pencil" is neither card text nor an artworkPrompt image word for The Notebook.
With opener "Yet the Censor's door" the beat runs 117 characters, beyond one breath; beats 3 and 31 also exceed 100.
"losing a tooth in a dream, not dentists; losing your power" breaks the card's grammar; the logic of the claim gets lost aloud.
Callback "But the Wish's teeth" exists, but its twist into The Hat has no causal link; it reads attached, not motivated.
